subject: Subset of nodes not updating when using dmulti

messages.author: c4f557fbb8021162
messages.subject: Subset of nodes not updating when using dmulti
parts:
Dear NIMBLE-Team,

I have recently been working on the implementation of a somewhat more complex integrated population model using NIMBLE.
Unlike other such models I worked with previously, this one includes not just two potential transitions for individuals in the population (i.e. survive or die), but multiple (i.e. transition to >2 states possible).
As such, I am implementing the process model using multinomial likelihoods. However, I have run into a problem where some (but not all!) of the stochastic nodes described by the multinomial likelihood are not updated at all (they simply remain "stuck" at the initial values).

No matter what I tried, I could not get these nodes to update and have a feeling I must be missing something important here. It would be fantastic if you could take a look into the problem and help me out!

I have made a reproducible example of the problem, and upload it here.
Below, I'll write down some more information on the specific problem.

Any tips/suggestions would be much appreciated!

Cheers,

Chloé



********************************************************************************************************
ADDITIONAL INFO ON PROBLEM:

In the process model, population size and structure are represented as N[zo, zt, t], where zt is the current state ("target state"), zo is the previous state ("origin state").
For the example (and the IPM application I am working on), states 1-3 are alive individuals, while states 4-9 are different "types" of dead individuals.
This means that only individuals in states 1, 2, and 3 at time t can contribute to population size at time t+1.
In the model, I specify this as:

    for(z in 1:3){
        N[z, 1:9, t+1] ~ dmulti(p = U[z, 1:9, t], size = sum(N[1:3, z, t]))
    }

When t <= Tmax, all nodes N[z, 4:9, t] are being updated, but all nodes N[z, 1:3, t] are not and remain "stuck" at the same values.
This happens irrespective of whether initial values are provided for N, and independent of assumptions about prior distribution of initial numbers (N[z, 1:9, 1])
Funnily enough, at the last time-step, all nodes N[z, 1:9, Tmax+1] are updated.

In the example, I provide the transition probabilities U as data. In the practical implementation (the integrated population model), U and (parts of) N are estimated from data.
However, the problem of "stuck" nodes is exactly the same there, so I assume if it can be "fixed" in the small example I provide, it can also be fixed in the integrated model.

Side note:
I ran the example using R 4.0.0 and nimble_0.9.0

messages.author: bebd85531a67ef86
messages.subject: Re: Subset of nodes not updating when using dmulti
parts:
Hi Chloé

As far as I can see, the problem appears to arise from the auto-correlation generated by the markovian dynamics of your model. Adding time to your code chunk (as you do in your file) we have this...

for(t in 1:Tmax){

for(z in 1:3){
        N[z, 1:9, t+1] ~ dmulti(p = U[z, 1:9, t], size = sum(N[1:3, z, t]))
    }

}

The sampler for multinomial nodes performs Metropolis-Hastings updates, i.e. it will propose an alternative vector for N[z, 1:9, t+1], evaluate the likelihood, and accept/reject based on the Metropolis-Hastings ratio. 

With your model, when a sampler generates a proposal for N[z, 1:9, t], it will be very likely that it will generate a new value for the "size" argument in the following time step, i.e. sum(N[1:3, z, t+1]). But if that value changes then the multinomial likelihood of the following timestep is no longer valid. So the proposal will be rejected. 

To illustrate this consider the following R code

> (r <- rmultinom(1, size=10, prob=1:4))
     [,1]
[1,]    2
[2,]    1
[3,]    3
[4,]    4
> dmultinom(r, size=10, prob=1:4)
[1] 0.01741824
> dmultinom(r, size=11, prob=1:4)
Error in dmultinom(r, size = 11, prob = 1:4) : 
  size != sum(x), i.e. one is wrong
> dmultinom(r, size=9, prob=1:4)
Error in dmultinom(r, size = 9, prob = 1:4) : 
  size != sum(x), i.e. one is wrong
 
So the default sampler for your multinomial nodes does not stand a chance. You will need an alternative way to generate proposals that can account for the autocorrelation in your model.  

David

messages.author: c4f557fbb8021162
messages.subject: Re: Subset of nodes not updating when using dmulti
parts:
Hi David!

Thank you very much for your reply, this makes a lot of sense.
It also explains why I only got this issue when using the multinomial likelihood with a "size" that is estimated (when "size" is a fixed constant, i.e. given as data, there was no problem).

I am now wondering what would be the best way to go about circumventing this problem.
From my view, this can be approached either by changing the samplers, or changing the model structure.

Samplers:
I assume none of the other "pre-programmed" samplers in the r-nimble package would be able to deal with this? Could there be a solution involving block sampling?
Surely, some samplers for autoregressive multinomial likelihoods must have been developed? Is anyone aware of examples?
I would greatly appreciate any pointers towards already existing solutions, or for building a custom sampler to deal with this.

Model structure:
Alternatively, getting rid of the autoregressive multinomial likelihood may solve the problem.
The obvious way of doing this seems to be rewriting the model as sequential (and conditional) binomial likelihoods. However, this is not just inelegant, but kind of defeats the purpose of what we would like to do with this model in practice ("general" integrated population model allowing for >2 transitions conditional on survival).
Are there any alternative formulations for the model that I may not be thinking of at the moment?

Any thoughts, ideas, and references (from anyone!) very welcome!

Cheers,

Chloé

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Subset of nodes not updating when using dmulti
parts:
Hi Chloe,

I've given this a little more thought.  I think I see the purpose of how you have set things up.  Unfortunately, it does not seem like an easy problem to solve. The current dmulti sampler conditions on size.  I think an update at one step could make the next step impossible by creating a mismatch between the size of the dmulti and the resulting states.  For example, if N[z, 1:9, t] is updated in a way that moves some individuals from alive states to dead states, then sum(N[1:3, z, t]) will no longer match the sum of the random variable it defines, namely sum(N[z, 1:9, t+1]).  I don't know if you've made any progress reformulating the model based on the twitter thread.  I imagine it would be possible to sample this model with a custom sampler that respects the constraints involved.   I don't think a vanilla block sampler will work.

-Perry

messages.author: bebd85531a67ef86
messages.subject: Re: Subset of nodes not updating when using dmulti
parts:
Just a couple of quick thoughts.

I imagine it should be possible to set up a sampler for sampling a series of dependant multinomial nodes. I suggest this is written as a separate chunk of code so that the current sampler remains unchanged. In which case there would (ideally) need to be some complimentary work on how nimble chooses between the current sampler and a sequential-multinomial sampler (that said, a user can always modify which samplers are being use manually). 

Chloé, will the number of time steps remain the same or be much bigger in your final model? This is an important detail, because, whilst the tailored (sequential-multinomial) sampler idea might work OK for a modest number of time steps, it's performance can be expected to decline as the number of time steps increases. In which case an approach based on particle MCMC (PMCMC) is probably more appropriate. I've not checked to see if nimble's current PMCMC functionality is capable of handling multinomial nodes. 

Best
David

messages.subject: Re: Subset of nodes not updating when using dmulti
parts:
Hi Chloe and David,

Sorry, this fell by the wayside indeed during vISEC2020.

The PMCMC implementation can handle vector state dynamics.  However, if observed numbers of observable states are error-free, then particle filtering methods can be problematic because the chance of a simulation hitting the observations can be low.  I am not sure if that is the case.

I do have ideas about samplers for the model with multinomial state dynamics.  While we like to keep discussions general and open on the list, I wonder if this will involve extended discussion of a somewhat narrow topic and is best taken off-list.  We can report back for interested list readers later.

-Perry

I've given this a little more thought.  I think I see the purpose of how you have set things up.  Unfortunately, it does not seem like an easy problem to solve. The current dmulti sampler conditions on size.  I think an update at one step could make the next step impossible by creating a mismatch between the size of the dmulti and the resulting states.  For example, if N[z, 1:9, t] is updated in a way that moves some individuals from alive states to dead states, then sum(N[1:3, z, t]) will no longer match the sum of the random variable it defines, namely sum(N[z, 1:9, t+1]).  I don't know if you've made any progress reformulating the model based on the twitter thread.  I imagine it would be possible to sample this model with a custom sampler that respects the constraints involved.   I don't think a vanilla block sampler will work.

-Perry

On Thu, Jun 18, 2020 at 4:49 AM Chloe Nater <gani...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi David!

Thank you very much for your reply, this makes a lot of sense.
It also explains why I only got this issue when using the multinomial likelihood with a "size" that is estimated (when "size" is a fixed constant, i.e. given as data, there was no problem).

I am now wondering what would be the best way to go about circumventing this problem.
From my view, this can be approached either by changing the samplers, or changing the model structure.

Samplers:
I assume none of the other "pre-programmed" samplers in the r-nimble package would be able to deal with this? Could there be a solution involving block sampling?
Surely, some samplers for autoregressive multinomial likelihoods must have been developed? Is anyone aware of examples?
I would greatly appreciate any pointers towards already existing solutions, or for building a custom sampler to deal with this.

Model structure:
Alternatively, getting rid of the autoregressive multinomial likelihood may solve the problem.
The obvious way of doing this seems to be rewriting the model as sequential (and conditional) binomial likelihoods. However, this is not just inelegant, but kind of defeats the purpose of what we would like to do with this model in practice ("general" integrated population model allowing for >2 transitions conditional on survival).
Are there any alternative formulations for the model that I may not be thinking of at the moment?

Any thoughts, ideas, and references (from anyone!) very welcome!

Cheers,

Chloé
